examShortTricks: Trick 1: Kipp's equation: FeS + H2SO4(dil) → FeSO4 + H2S↑ — apparatus works by stopcock-controlled contact between acid and FeS in the middle bulb; draw the three-bulb shape.
Trick 2: Acidic nature: 2H2S ⇌ 2H+ + S2−, a weak diprotic acid — reacts with bases to give two series of salts (HS− and S2−).
Trick 3: Reducing nature equations: H2S + Cl2 → 2HCl + S (decoulourises Cl2 water); 2H2S + SO2 → 3S + 2H2O; H2S turns acidified KMnO4 colourless.
Trick 4: Analytical use: group II cation sulphides are coloured — PbS black, CdS yellow, ZnS white; 'H2S in qualitative analysis' is the use to quote.
